name: Fairmont Scottsdale Princess
positioning: Large Southwestern-style desert resort in North Scottsdale, next to the TPC Scottsdale golf complex, with a Sisley-Paris spa and several pools
best_for: Golfers who want to stay next to the TPC Scottsdale complex
Families who want kid-focused pools and a supervised kids club

facts.text: The resort has grand Mexican Colonial architecture stretching across 65 acres of the Sonoran Desert.
The resort is adjacent to the TPC Scottsdale complex, home to the PGA Tour's WM Phoenix Open.
Toro, in the clubhouse of the TPC course, serves Latin American fare blended with Japanese offerings and has a patio overlooking the fairway and the McDowell Mountains.
The resort also has Ironwood American Kitchen, Plaza Bar and Michael Mina's Bourbon Steak.
The spa's locker rooms have steam rooms, dry saunas, hot tubs and cold plunges, and the spa has a rooftop pool.
The Sunset Beach pool has sand imported from Florida, and a supervised kids club for ages 5 through 12 is available for an extra cost.
Fairmont View rooms have a balcony with golf course views.
Fairmont Gold Jr Suites include lounge access with complimentary breakfast.
The resort is in North Scottsdale, an upscale suburban area, a few miles from high-end shopping and dining complexes.

highlights.text: The Sisley-Paris Spa is a spa within the resort's spa and is one of the few Sisley outposts in the country.
The Sonoran Splash pool is geared toward kids and has twisting water slides.
Chef Richard Sandoval is behind two of the resort's restaurants.
Privado Studio villas have a private entrance, a gas fireplace and a soaking bathtub.

considerations.text: The resort is massive and draws a cross section of guests, including many business travelers attending conferences.
Condé Nast Traveler says the resort's size means service is attentive and prompt but not intimate.
WhataHotel notes the large property can require a shuttle or a long walk between areas.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: Fairmont Scottsdale Princess
